title: 25 billion payments a month, and they're free. Who pays for India's UPI? #shorts
description:
India's UPI handled about 25.5 billion payments worth ₹31.53 lakh crore in October 2026 (about ₹1,238 per payment on average), and customers pay nothing. Since 2020 the law has kept the merchant fee (MDR) at zero, the government has paid banks an incentive on small shop payments, and apps earn from loans, insurance and shop devices instead. In September 2026, NPCI announced a 0.4% fee on shop payments above ₹2,000 (capped at ₹300, paid by merchants, not customers); its 15 October start was deferred and no new date had been announced as of 20 November 2026.

Sources: NPCI monthly UPI statistics, October 2026 (reported 1-2 Nov 2026); PIB / Ministry of Finance, '₹1,500 Cr Incentive Scheme for Low-Value BHIM-UPI Transactions' (24 Mar 2025); NPCI FAQs on MDR on select UPI P2M transactions (15 Sep 2026); Business Today (20 Nov 2026) on the deferral; PhonePe updated DRHP (Mar 2026); Paytm Q2 FY27 results (27 Oct 2026).

scenes.say: In October alone, Indians made over twenty-five billion UPI payments, and paid nothing to send them. So who pays?
UPI is India's instant payment system. Scan a shop's QR code, and money moves straight from your bank to theirs.
Normally, shops pay a fee on card sales. In India, a debit card can cost up to zero point nine percent. UPI costs zero, by law, since twenty twenty.
But running UPI isn't free. NPCI cites estimates of twenty thousand crore rupees a year. The government's incentive to banks for twenty twenty-four to twenty-five? Fifteen hundred crore.
So apps like PhonePe and PayTM make money elsewhere: loans, insurance, and payment speakers rented to shops.
And free may not last. India has announced a zero point four percent fee on shop payments over two thousand rupees, paid by the shop, not you. Its start has been delayed.
